Definition: from the same as G154; causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer:--author.
BiblicalUsage: Once, and it is one of the weightiest verses in Hebrews: Christ, being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him. The word is causer — the one who brings something about.
TheologicalSignificance: One word, one verse, and the word itself is only a label — causer; its weight is the verse, Christ made the author of eternal salvation, and that weight belongs to the verse, not the word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
